top_news.title: What Does 99% Accuracy Measure? A Reproducible Audit of Shortcut Learning in a Widely Used Fake News Corpus
top_news.dek: Researchers find that the popular ISOT/Kaggle fake news corpus is fundamentally flawed due to metadata leakage.
top_news.brief: An audit of the widely used ISOT/Kaggle fake news dataset reveals that high accuracy scores are driven by shortcut learning rather than linguistic analysis. A simple classifier using only subject metadata achieved 100% F1, proving the benchmark is degenerate and unsuitable for evaluating model veracity.
top_news.image_alt: Chart showing accuracy drop when metadata is removed from the dataset

top_news.title: Show HN: Training a model to identify AI web content from structure alone
top_news.dek: SlopShape uses structural analysis to detect AI-generated commercial content.
top_news.brief: Researchers have developed SlopShape, a method that identifies AI-generated commercial content by analyzing structural signatures rather than word-level patterns. By examining information flow, evidence presentation, and voice, the model successfully distinguishes between human-written blog posts and AI-generated mirrors across five frontier models.
top_news.image_alt: Visualization of structural patterns in AI vs human text

primary.title: Inside Basecamp Research, the AI startup turning evolution into training data
primary.summary: Basecamp Research has raised $140 million from investors including Nvidia and Anthropic's Anthology Fund. The London company trains AI models on genetic material from rainforests, oceans, and hot springs to design antibiotics and tools for cell therapies. In an interview with THE DECODER, CTO Philip Lorenz explains why biology is a far bigger problem for AI than language, and why good scores on paper don't guarantee good molecules.
